title: Kieran Culkin Rejects Succession Spinoff Idea, Teases Jesse Armstrong Film
excerpt:
The actor behind Roman Roy believes Succession ended exactly where it should.
He also revealed plans to reunite with creator Jesse Armstrong on a film.
body_md:
Three years after Succession concluded, Kieran Culkin has made his position on a possible spinoff clear: he does not think the Roy family needs another television chapter. The actor, who played Roman Roy throughout the HBO drama's four seasons, discussed the idea during an appearance on Heart Breakfast while promoting The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Asked whether the acclaimed drama could return in another form, Culkin dismissed the suggestion and joked about the prospect of a sitcom built around Cousin Greg. His remark referenced Greg Hirsch, played by Nicholas Braun, and the character's memorable relationship with Tom Wambsgans, portrayed by Matthew Macfadyen. Their alliance became a recurring source of comedy and tension amid the series' corporate power struggles.

Culkin's reluctance to revisit Succession does not mean he has lost affection for Roman. He acknowledged missing the character and said creator Jesse Armstrong had previously described three possible directions for a fifth season. Once Culkin understood the ending of season four, however, he felt the story had reached the right conclusion.

The series ended in 2023, leaving audiences to consider what might happen next to the Roy siblings after their fight for control of Waystar Royco. For Culkin, those lingering questions do not automatically justify reopening the narrative. His comments are an actor's assessment, not an announcement of a network decision, and the report does not confirm any new season or spinoff commission.

There is nevertheless another collaboration on the horizon. Culkin said he is preparing to work with Armstrong on a film for which the Succession creator has written a script. He did not disclose a title, plot, production schedule or release date. Armstrong previously directed Mountainhead for HBO, a dark comedy about wealthy friends navigating a crisis tied to their own actions.

The conversation also touched on Culkin's earlier role as Fuller McCallister in the first two Home Alone movies. He said he still watches Home Alone around Christmas. Although speculation about the franchise's future continues, there is no confirmation in this report that Culkin will reprise Fuller. The concrete development from his interview is his stated intention to reunite professionally with Armstrong, not a return to Succession.
seo_title: Kieran Culkin on Succession Spinoff and New Film
seo_description: Kieran Culkin says Succession ended perfectly, rejects a spinoff and discusses a planned film with Jesse Armstrong.
